explanation: Job 1 incorrectly omitted the qualifying record n06-r06. The top-level corpus includes n06-r06 with demand_score 5, so it qualifies under the stated selection rule and the visible select_demand condition. However job_1 output contains only seven needs and evidence_sources and excludes n06-r06. The visible normalize function restricts retained records to an allowed_record_ids list that contains n06-r09 instead of n06-r06, causing n06-r06 to be silently dropped before the downstream handoff. Job 2 then preserves the faulty upstream handoff, so the downstream omission is propagated rather than introduced there.
cited_evidence: Behavioural criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and preserving record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight.
Top-level corpus contains {'record_id':'n06-r06','need':'compare selected and complete runtime evidence','demand_score':5,'source_id':'s06','source_weight':3}.
select_demand source selects rows where demand_score >= 3 or record_id is in fallback_ids, so n06-r06 qualifies.
job_1 output needs and evidence_sources omit n06-r06 and report record_count/evidence_source_count as 7.
normalize source uses allowed_record_ids = ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'], which excludes n06-r06 and includes non-input n06-r09.
